description.narrative:
IFC anticipates that the Project will promote increased access to climate finance to retail customers and SMEs in Brazil, promoting the replacement of costly energy sources with lower-cost, solar-generated electricity. The attractive spread between the average electricity tariff and the levelized cost of electricity for solar will imply immediate cost savings upon installation of the solar panel.
Through IFC investment, Sol Agora is expected to support an expansion of around 90MW, thus contributing to the improvement of the carbon footprint of the power sector in Brazil. The Government of Brazil has committed to reducing the countrys GHG emissions by 50% compared to 2005 levels in 2030 under the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) submitted as part of the Paris Agreement. The Project will contribute to the countrys climate mitigation agenda by supporting, with a small footprint but directly, the displacement, particularly during draught events, of high-polluting thermal power sources such as coal and heavy fuel oil, with non-conventional renewable energy, hence reducing the associated carbon emissions.
IFC anticipates that the Project will help deepen the Brazilian FIDC market by supporting the nascent ESG-oriented FIDC sub-sector. Sol Agora FIDC is aligned with the Green Bond Principles and has received an SPO (Securitização de Performance Operacional Sustentável) from Bureau Veritas as a pure-play ESG vehicle. Only a few Green FIDCs are in operation in Brazil so far.

The proposed project (the Project) consists of a 9-year (including 1 year of grace period) investment of up to BRL 250 million investment in one or more series of senior quotas of Sol Agora Green II ESG FIDC (Sol Agora FIDC or the Fund), which is a non-recourse vehicle that provides long-term financing to diversified residential clients and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) for the acquisition and installation of micro and mini-distributed solar power generation assets in Brazil.
